skill.body:
# Mobile Development Skill — Quick Reference

This skill equips mobile developers with execution-ready patterns for building native and cross-platform mobile applications. Claude should apply these patterns when users ask for iOS/Android app architecture, UI components, navigation flows, API integration, offline storage, authentication, or mobile-specific features.

---

# When to Use This Skill

Claude should invoke this skill when a user requests:

- iOS app development (Swift, SwiftUI, UIKit)
- Android app development (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose)
- Cross-platform development (React Native, WebView)
- Mobile app architecture and patterns
- Navigation and routing
- State management (Redux, MobX, MVVM)
- Network requests and API integration
- Local data storage (Core Data, Room, SQLite)
- Authentication and session management
- Push notifications
- Camera and media access
- Location services
- App Store / Play Store deployment
- Mobile performance optimization
- Offline-first architecture

---

## Quick Reference Table

| Task | iOS | Android | Cross-Platform | When to Use |
|------|-----|---------|----------------|-------------|
| Native UI | SwiftUI + UIKit | Jetpack Compose + Views | React Native | Native: Best performance; Cross-platform: Code sharing |
| Navigation | NavigationStack | Navigation Component | React Navigation | Platform-specific for native feel |
| State Management | @State/@Observable | ViewModel + StateFlow | Redux/MobX | iOS: @Observable; Android: ViewModel; RN: Redux |
| Networking | URLSession + async/await | Retrofit + Coroutines | Axios/Fetch | Native: Type-safe; RN: JavaScript ecosystem |
| Local Storage | Core Data + SwiftData | Room Database | AsyncStorage/SQLite | Native: Full control; RN: Simpler |
| Push Notifications | APNs | FCM | React Native Firebase | Native: Platform-specific; RN: Unified API |

## Decision Tree: Platform Selection

```text
Need to build mobile app for: [Target Audience]
    ├─ iOS only?
    │   └─ Use Swift + SwiftUI (templates/swift/)
    │
    ├─ Android only?
    │   └─ Use Kotlin + Jetpack Compose (templates/kotlin/)
    │
    ├─ Both iOS and Android?
    │   ├─ Need maximum performance?
    │   │   └─ Build separate native apps (Swift + Kotlin)
    │   │
    │   ├─ Need faster development + code sharing?
    │   │   └─ Use React Native (templates/cross-platform/)
    │   │
    │   └─ Wrapping existing web app?
    │       └─ Use WebView wrapper (templates/cross-platform/template-webview.md)
```

---

generated_query: I’m building a mobile app for a local meal kit delivery service. The app should let users browse weekly menus (with photos, ingredients, and dietary tags), customize their box, place orders, and receive push notifications when their delivery is out for pickup. We need to target both iOS and Android, and I’d like to reuse as much code as possible to speed up development. The app must work offline for viewing past orders and saved menus. For payments, we’ll use Stripe. User authentication should be phone-based with OTP verification. Can you help me choose the right cross-platform framework and provide concrete code examples for: navigation between menu, cart, order history, and account screens; state management for the cart and user session; networking for fetching menus and submitting orders with proper error handling; local storage for offline access; integrating push notifications on both platforms; and securely storing authentication tokens? Also, I need guidance on handling the WebView flow for the payment gateway and barcode scanning for pickup verification. Finally, give me a checklist for app store and play store deployment.

# Mobile Development Skill — Quick Reference

This skill equips mobile developers with execution-ready patterns for building React Native applications. Claude should apply these patterns when users ask for cross-platform app architecture, UI components, navigation flows, API integration, and basic authentication.

---

# When to Use This Skill

Claude should invoke this skill when a user requests:

- Cross-platform app development (React Native)
- Navigation and routing between screens
- State management (Redux, Zustand, Context)
- Network requests and API integration
- Local storage for basic caching
- Authentication with token-based flows
- Push notifications (optional – requires native setup)
- App Store / Play Store deployment
- Camera and media access

**Note**: This skill is optimized for React Native with Expo. For platform-specific native features (barcode scanning, WebView payment flows) see the WebView and Camera templates.

---

## Quick Reference Table

| Task | React Native (Expo) | Alternative | When to Use |
|------|---------------------|-------------|-------------|
| Navigation | React Navigation | React Router Native | Stack/Tab/Bottom Tab patterns |
| State Management | Context + useReducer | Redux Toolkit / Zustand | Context for small apps, Redux for complex |
| Networking | Axios + useState/useEffect | React Query / SWR | Axios for simple APIs, React Query for caching |
| Local Storage | AsyncStorage | Expo SQLite / SecureStore | Simple key-value for caching; SecureStore for tokens |
| Push Notifications | Expo Notifications | FCM/APNs via bare workflow | Expo handles both platforms under the hood |
| Camera/Media | Expo Camera / ImagePicker | react-native-vision-camera | For photo capture or QR scanning |

---

## Decision Tree: Framework Selection

```text
Need to build mobile app for: [Target Audience]
    ├─ Only need one platform?
    │   └─ Use Swift or Kotlin (see other skill documents)
    │
    ├─ Both iOS and Android?
    │   ├─ Want rapid development + code sharing?
    │   │   └─ Use React Native with Expo (this skill)
    │   │
    │   └─ Need maximum native performance?
    │       └─ Build separate native apps (not covered here)
    │
    └─ Wrapping existing web app?
        └─ Use WebView component in React Native (template-webview.md)
```

---

## Navigation & Screen Structure

- **Templates**: [templates/cross-platform/template-navigation.md](templates/cross-platform/template-navigation.md) – Stack, Tab, and Drawer navigation examples with React Navigation.
- **Resources**: [resources/react-native-best-practices.md](resources/react-native-best-practices.md) – Performance tips, caching strategies, and Expo build configuration.

---

## State Management

For cart and user session, use React Context with useReducer or Zustand. Avoid storing large objects in AsyncStorage.

**Template**: [templates/cross-platform/template-state-management.md](templates/cross-platform/template-state-management.md)

---

## Networking

Axios with interceptors for token injection and error handling. React Query for automatic caching and background refetching.

**Template**: [templates/cross-platform/template-networking.md](templates/cross-platform/template-networking.md)

---

## Local Storage & Offline

Basic offline support via AsyncStorage for caching menus and past orders. For full offline-first architecture, consider SQLite or WatermelonDB (not covered in this skill).

**Template**: [templates/cross-platform/template-local-storage.md](templates/cross-platform/template-local-storage.md)

---

## Push Notifications

Expo Notifications provides a unified API. Requires a server component for trigger; client-side setup is straightforward.

**Template**: [templates/cross-platform/template-push-notifications.md](templates/cross-platform/template-push-notifications.md)

---

## Authentication

Phone-based OTP: Use Firebase Authentication or a custom backend with token exchange. Secure token storage with Expo SecureStore.

**Template**: [templates/cross-platform/template-authentication.md](templates/cross-platform/template-authentication.md)

---

## WebView & Payment

For Stripe payments, use a WebView component to load the Stripe Checkout page. This skill covers basic WebView embedding; advanced redirect handling is in the WebView template.

**Template**: [templates/cross-platform/template-webview.md](templates/cross-platform/template-webview.md)

---

## Barcode Scanning

Use Expo Camera with `barCodeScanner` prop for pickup verification. Works on both platforms with minimal code.

**Template**: [templates/cross-platform/template-camera-barcode.md](templates/cross-platform/template-camera-barcode.md)

---

## Deployment Checklist

- Build with `eas build` for iOS and Android
- Configure app icons, splash screens, and versioning
- Test on physical devices
- Submit to App Store Connect and Google Play Console
- (Optional) Set up crash reporting with Sentry

**Full checklist**: [resources/deployment-checklist.md](resources/deployment-checklist.md)

---

## Related Skills

- [../software-testing-automation/SKILL.md](../software-testing-automation/SKILL.md) – Mobile CI and testing
- [../software-frontend/SKILL.md](../software-frontend/SKILL.md) – Web UI patterns for hybrid apps

# Mobile Development Skill — Quick Reference

This skill equips mobile developers with execution-ready patterns for building native iOS and Android applications. Claude should apply these patterns when users ask for platform-specific app architecture, UI components, navigation flows, API integration, or authentication.

---

## When to Use This Skill

Claude should invoke this skill when a user requests:

- iOS app development (Swift, SwiftUI, UIKit)
- Android app development (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose)
- Native navigation and routing
- State management (MVVM, Combine)
- Network requests and API integration
- Basic local data storage (UserDefaults, SharedPreferences)
- Authentication and session management
- Location services
- Mobile performance optimization

---

## Quick Reference Table

| Task | iOS | Android | Notes |
|------|-----|---------|-------|
| UI | SwiftUI + UIKit | Jetpack Compose + Views | Follow platform HIG/Material Design |
| Navigation | NavigationStack/UINavigationController | Navigation Component | Standard patterns |
| State Management | @State @Observable | ViewModel + StateFlow | Per-screen data flow |
| Networking | URLSession (async/await) | Retrofit + Coroutines | Request/response error handling |
| Local Storage | UserDefaults, Keychain | SharedPreferences, EncryptedSharedPrefs | Simple key-value persistence |
| Authentication | ASWebAuthenticationSession | Custom Tabs / Firebase Auth | OAuth flows |

## Decision Tree: Platform Selection

```text
Need to build mobile app for: [Target Audience]
    ├─ iOS only?
    │   └─ Use Swift + SwiftUI (templates/swift/)
    ├─ Android only?
    │   └─ Use Kotlin + Jetpack Compose (templates/kotlin/)
    └─ Both iOS and Android?
        └─ Build separate native apps for best performance and platform fidelity
```

---

## Navigation

**iOS (SwiftUI)**
- Use `NavigationStack` with `NavigationLink` for stack-based flows
- Example: menu → cart → order history → account

```swift
struct ContentView: View {
    var body: some View {
        NavigationStack {
            MenuView()
                .navigationDestination(for: Route.self) { route in
                    switch route {
                    case .cart: CartView()
                    case .history: HistoryView()
                    case .account: AccountView()
                    }
                }
        }
    }
}
```

**Android (Jetpack Compose)**
- Use `NavHost` with `composable` routes
- Example: menu → cart → history → account

```kotlin
@Composable
fun AppNavigation() {
    val navController = rememberNavController()
    NavHost(navController, startDestination = "menu") {
        composable("menu") { MenuView(navController) }
        composable("cart") { CartView(navController) }
        composable("history") { HistoryView(navController) }
        composable("account") { AccountView(navController) }
    }
}
```

---

## State Management

**iOS**
- Use `@Observable` class for cart and user session
- Share via `@Environment` or dependency injection

**Android**
- Use ViewModel + StateFlow per screen
- Share state via shared ViewModel scoped to nav graph

---

## Networking

**iOS (URLSession + async/await)**
- Create a reusable `APIClient` with `URLSession`
- Handle errors with `do/catch` and custom error types

**Android (Retrofit + Coroutines)**
- Define an interface with suspend functions
- Use `Result` wrapper for error handling

---

## Authentication (Phone OTP)

**iOS**
- Use Firebase Authentication or a custom SMS gateway
- Store token in Keychain

**Android**
- Use Firebase Phone Auth or a custom OTP SDK
- Store token in EncryptedSharedPreferences

---

## WebView for Payments

Integrate Stripe via a standard WebView. Load the payment URL and handle deep links for success/cancelation.

```swift
// iOS
WebView(request: paymentURLRequest)
    .navigationBarHidden(true)
    .onOpenURL { url in handlePaymentResult(url) }
```

```kotlin
// Android
AndroidView(factory = { context ->
    WebView(context).apply {
        webViewClient = object : WebViewClient() {
            override fun shouldOverrideUrlLoading(view: WebView?, request: WebResourceRequest?): Boolean {
                // intercept stripe return URLs
                return false
            }
        }
        loadUrl(paymentUrl)
    }
})
```

---

## Deployment Notes

- iOS: Certificate, Provisioning Profile, App Store Connect setup, TestFlight
- Android: Signing key, Google Play Console, internal/alpha/beta tracks

Refer to platform-specific documentation for detailed steps.

---

## Templates

- iOS: [templates/swift/template-swift.md](templates/swift/template-swift.md)
- Android: [templates/kotlin/template-kotlin.md](templates/kotlin/template-kotlin.md)
- Cross-platform: not recommended for complex native features

---

# Mobile Development Skill — Quick Reference

This skill equips mobile developers with execution-ready patterns for building cross-platform mobile applications using React Native and WebView wrappers. Claude should apply these patterns when users ask for app architecture, UI components, navigation flows, API integration, or authentication.

---

# When to Use This Skill

Claude should invoke this skill when a user requests:

- Cross-platform mobile app development (React Native, Expo)
- WebView-based hybrid apps
- Navigation and routing between screens
- State management (Redux)
- Network requests and API integration
- Basic local caching
- Authentication (email/password, OAuth)
- Push notifications (via FCM)
- App Store / Play Store deployment basics
- Camera access (for photo capture)
- Location services

---

## Quick Reference Table

| Task | React Native (Recommended) | WebView Wrapper | When to Use |
|------|----------------------------|-----------------|-------------|
| UI | React Native Components | HTML/CSS/JS | React Native for native feel; WebView for web-first |
| Navigation | React Navigation | Browser history | React Navigation for stack/tab layouts |
| State Management | Redux Toolkit | Context API | Redux for complex state; Context for simple apps |
| Networking | Axios | Fetch API | Axios for interceptor support |
| Local Caching | MMKV | AsyncStorage | MMKV for performance; AsyncStorage for strings |
| Push Notifications | Firebase Cloud Messaging | Not available | FCM for Android/iOS |
| Authentication | Firebase Auth / JWT tokens | Server-side session | Firebase for ease; JWT for custom backends |

## Decision Tree: Platform Selection

```text
Need to build mobile app for: [Target Audience]
    ├─ Both iOS and Android?
    │   └─ Use React Native with Expo (templates/cross-platform/)
    │
    ├─ Wrapping existing web app?
    │   └─ Use WebView wrapper (templates/cross-platform/template-webview.md)
    │
    ├─ Need maximum native features?
    │   └─ Consider native iOS or Android (not covered in this skill)
```

---

## Navigation

- Use React Navigation with `@react-navigation/native` and `@react-navigation/stack`.
- Define stack navigator for main screens: Home, Cart, Orders, Account.
- Use `NavigationContainer` at root.

Example:
```javascript
import { NavigationContainer } from '@react-navigation/native';
import { createStackNavigator } from '@react-navigation/stack';

const Stack = createStackNavigator();

function App() {
  return (
    <NavigationContainer>
      <Stack.Navigator>
        <Stack.Screen name="Home" component={HomeScreen} />
        <Stack.Screen name="Cart" component={CartScreen} />
        <Stack.Screen name="Orders" component={OrderHistoryScreen} />
        <Stack.Screen name="Account" component={AccountScreen} />
      </Stack.Navigator>
    </NavigationContainer>
  );
}
```

## State Management (Cart & Session)

- Use Redux Toolkit for global state (cart items, user session).
- Define slices for `cart` and `auth`.
- Persist Redux state using `redux-persist` with `MMKV` storage for fast reads.

Example cart slice:
```javascript
import { createSlice } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';

const cartSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'cart',
  initialState: { items: [] },
  reducers: {
    addItem: (state, action) => { state.items.push(action.payload); },
    removeItem: (state, action) => { state.items = state.items.filter(i => i.id !== action.payload); }
  }
});
```

## Networking

- Use Axios with interceptors for token injection and error handling.
- Define base URL from environment variables.
- Handle network errors with try/catch and show user-friendly messages.

```javascript
import axios from 'axios';

const api = axios.create({ baseURL: 'https://api.example.com' });

api.interceptors.request.use(config => {
  const token = store.getState().auth.token;
  if (token) config.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`;
  return config;
});

export const fetchMenus = async () => {
  try {
    const response = await api.get('/menus');
    return response.data;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Failed to fetch menus:', error);
    throw new Error('Unable to load menus. Please try again later.');
  }
};
```

## Authentication

- Use Firebase Authentication with email/password for simplicity.
- Alternatively, implement JWT-based auth with a custom backend.
- Store tokens securely using `react-native-keychain` or Expo's `SecureStore`.
- Provide login and registration screens; use OTP only if explicitly required (not covered here).

## Local Storage (Caching)

- Use MMKV for key-value storage of user preferences and session tokens.
- For larger structured data (menus, past orders), use `expo-sqlite` or `redux-persist`.
- Offline support is not built-in; require internet for fetching menus and placing orders.

## Push Notifications

- Integrate Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) using `@react-native-firebase/messaging`.
- Request notification permissions on first launch.
- Handle incoming notifications with a local notification library (e.g., `@notifee/react-native`).
- Delivery notifications: send via backend to FCM topic or individual device tokens.

## Deployment Checklist (App Store & Play Store)

- [ ] Create app icons and splash screens for all required sizes.
- [ ] Generate signed APK/AAB for Android using Android Studio.
- [ ] Build iOS archive via Xcode and upload to App Store Connect.
- [ ] Prepare privacy policy and terms of service URLs.
- [ ] Set up Firebase project for push notifications and analytics.
- [ ] Run UI tests on multiple device sizes.
- [ ] Submit for review; handle common rejection issues (e.g., incomplete metadata).

# Mobile Development Skill — Quick Reference

This skill equips mobile developers with execution-ready patterns for building native and cross-platform mobile applications. Claude should apply these patterns when users ask for iOS/Android app architecture, UI components, navigation flows, API integration, offline storage, authentication, or mobile-specific features.

---

# When to Use This Skill

Claude should invoke this skill when a user requests:

- iOS app development (Swift, SwiftUI, UIKit)
- Android app development (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose)
- Cross-platform development (React Native, WebView)
- Mobile app architecture and patterns
- Navigation and routing
- State management (Redux, MobX, MVVM)
- Network requests and API integration
- Local data storage (Core Data, Room, SQLite)
- Authentication and session management
- Push notifications
- Camera and media access
- Location services
- App Store / Play Store deployment
- Mobile performance optimization
- Cache invalidation basics

---

## Quick Reference Table

| Task | iOS | Android | Cross-Platform | When to Use |
|------|-----|---------|----------------|-------------|
| Native UI | SwiftUI + UIKit | Jetpack Compose + Views | React Native | Native: Best performance; Cross-platform: Code sharing |
| Navigation | NavigationStack | Navigation Component | React Navigation | Platform-specific for native feel |
| State Management | @State/@Observable | ViewModel + StateFlow | Redux/MobX | iOS: @Observable; Android: ViewModel; RN: Redux |
| Networking | URLSession + async/await | Retrofit + Coroutines | Axios/Fetch | Native: Type-safe; RN: JavaScript ecosystem |
| Local Storage | Core Data + SwiftData | Room Database | AsyncStorage (basic key-value) | In-memory caching is also supported |
| Push Notifications | APNs | FCM | React Native Firebase | Native: Platform-specific; RN: Unified API |

## Decision Tree: Platform Selection

```text
Need to build mobile app for: [Target Audience]
    ├─ iOS only?
    │   └─ Use Swift + SwiftUI (templates/swift/)
    │
    ├─ Android only?
    │   └─ Use Kotlin + Jetpack Compose (templates/kotlin/)
    │
    ├─ Both iOS and Android?
    │   ├─ Need maximum performance?
    │   │   └─ Build separate native apps (Swift + Kotlin)
    │   │
    │   ├─ Need faster development + code sharing?
    │   │   └─ Use React Native (templates/cross-platform/)
    │   │
    │   └─ Wrapping existing web app?
    │       └─ Use WebView wrapper (templates/cross-platform/template-webview.md)
```
